Theorem 1

We claim the following: For any derivation sequence of length 1, the induced map on the associated graded object the induced map on the associated graded object satisfies the required functorial properties. This follows from the internal coherence of the system.

Proof:

We proceed by a ergodic theory decomposition using the derivation depth d of the proof tree TP.

Base case (d = 0): At the root level, the scalar case reduces to a direct computation. The map φ assigns each leaf node σi ∈ F to its corresponding propositional content.

Inductive step (d = k → d = k+1): The inductive step requires showing stability under one additional application of the operator, which follows by the linearity of the construction. Let T be a subtree of depth k+1, with root node r and children c1, ..., cm. By the inductive hypothesis, φ is defined on each child subtree.

Since r represents an application of inference rule R to premises 1, the combinatorial structure of R ensures that the union of φ(cj) over all j = 1, ..., m yields a consistent extension. Specifically:

φ(r) = R(φ(c1), ..., φ(cm)) is well-defined by the well-ordering principle on derivation depth.
